📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

United Launch Alliance stated Wednesday that the failure of its Vulcan rocket during a launch on Sunday was caused by inadequate fuel supply.

According to recent reports, “ULA has completed an initial integrated review of flight data from the Leo 1 launch anomaly that occurred last Sunday,” the organization stated in a statement. “While work remains to determine cause, preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines.”.

The latest information released by ULA confirms reporting from Ars Technica on Tuesday that the rocket’s failure was not due to the performance of the vehicle’s main engines, which are provided by Blue Origin.

This represents an important revelation from ULA and will provide some major relief to different parts of the US aerospace community, particularly Blue Origin and NASA.

That’s because the BE-4 engine is also the bedrock of Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket. This powerful rocket uses a similar but slightly more powerful version of the BE-4 engine. New Glenn experienced its own catastrophic failure in May during a ground test, a failure that was later attributed to a main oxygen valve on one of the BE-4 engines.

After this anomaly, Blue Origin retrofitted the main oxygen valve, including for Vulcan missions. Now it’s clear that this retrofit was not implicated in the Vulcan accident. With the preliminary Vulcan investigation having largely exonerated the BE-4 engine, Blue Origin can press ahead with its return-to-flight mission with Latest Glenn, which could occur as soon as January.

“Following the Vulcan anomaly, Blue Origin immediately worked alongside ULA to review flight data and support the investigation,” Blue Origin remarked in a statement Wednesday. “Together, we identified that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines. ULA is a valued partner, and we look forward to Vulcan’s return to flight.”.

Amid a worsening US launch crunch, New Glenn offers the most tangible option for near-term relief for satellite operators, including Amazon Leo, which lost dozens of satellites on Sunday. The heavy-lift rocket has many commercial and government customers lined up for launch. NASA in particular is counting on the rocket to launch a number of lunar missions in the next two years, as well as play a significant role in landing humans on the Moon later this decade.

Also a relief to NASA will be confirmation that Vulcan’s upper stage, the Centaur V, did not contribute to the failure. NASA recently contracted with ULA to use the Centaur V as its new upper stage for the Space Launch System rocket, enabling future missions to the Moon.

For ULA, however, the latest revision only brings more challenges.

According to recent reports, vulcan represents the tech giant’s great hope to remain relevant in a US launch industry increasingly dominated by SpaceX and newer entrants such as Blue Origin. With Vulcan on the sidelines, other companies, such as Relativity Space, Rocket Lab, and Stoke Space, could also elbow out the once all-powerful launch firm.

Although Sunday’s Vulcan flight, its fifth overall, was the first outright mission failure for the rocket, two previous launches also experienced problems. Those issues involved the nozzle of the solid rocket boosters. ULA has now spent three years trying to move the rocket out of its teething phase and into regular operations. A successful launch on Sunday could have set up at least a monthly launch cadence next year.

Now, the cash-strapped tech giant must also contend with a new issue involving propellant management and complicated plumbing that feeds liquid oxygen and methane to the BE-4 engines. It will certainly be offline for several months.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Amazon CloudFront Functions can now make network calls and act on the response during a request.
  • Sources indicate that with the upcoming cf.fetch() method, your functions can call your API endpoints and use the response to decide how to handle each request.
  • Industry observers note that network calls are available at all CloudFront edge locations.

Amazon CloudFront Functions can now make network calls and act on the response during a request. CloudFront Functions runs lightweight JavaScript at CloudFront edge locations to customize requests and responses. Previously, if your logic depended on data from another service, you had to use Lambda@Edge or move that logic to your origin. Now your functions can use real-time data to personalize, authenticate, or route requests at the edge, close to your viewers.

Sources indicate that with the upcoming cf.fetch() method, your functions can call your API endpoints and use the response to decide how to handle each request. For example, you can check an AI agent's permissions and usage budget so that only authorized requests reach your API or MCP server, or send request signals to a security or fraud detection service to block or challenge bad traffic. With cf.beacon(), you can send analytics events in the background without slowing down viewers, even for content served from cache. Both methods take advantage of the origin settings already on your distribution, including origin access control (OAC), VPC origins, and connection reuse.

Industry observers note that network calls are available at all CloudFront edge locations. They cost $0.10 per million calls, on top of CloudFront Functions invocation charges, and are included at no additional cost in the Pro strategy and above in CloudFront flat-rate plans. To learn more, see Helper methods for network calls in the Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide and Amazon CloudFront pricing.

  • It has been revealed that but those intrusive thoughts never crossed my mind while I was testing Specialized’s Turbo Vado 3 Evo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve had only one experience of pedaling an e-bike after it ran out of juice, but it was enough to make checking the battery display an anxiety-driven habit: “Can I afford to use the highest assist level up this hill? Should I switch to eco mode to preserve power and make sure I have enough to get home with the bike lights on?”.

These aren’t fun questions to have rattling around in your head while riding home in the dark.

It has been revealed that but those intrusive thoughts never crossed my mind while I was testing Specialized’s Turbo Vado 3 Evo. I didn’t experience range anxiety, even while blowing through city streets at 25-plus mph (40.2 kph). The bike has so much juice (840 watt-hours) and power (810 watts of peak power and 105 newton-meters of torque) from Specialized’s 3.1 motor system that I could ride as far and as fast as I wanted without worrying about having enough battery to get back home.

Recent findings suggest that given my preference for biking over driving, I need a bike that can get me across town at a decent clip without draining an entire charge. That’s exactly what the Evo delivered on my longest rides.

Industry observers note that what sold me on the bike was a 24-mile round trip that took 83 minutes and used just 56 percent of the battery. According to Specialized’s app, which connects to the bike over Bluetooth, I averaged 235 W of assist power while moving an average of 17 mph, though I was generally closer to 20 mph on stretches where I didn’t have to slow down. I also hit a max speed of 27.3 mph with little effort.

The bike is a beast, weighing around 70 pounds for the large-size frame I tested. Despite being the heaviest e-bike I’ve ridden, the Evo makes pedaling easier than ever. The bike lacks a throttle, so it takes a few rotations to get moving, but once the assist kicks in, it’s remarkable how easily you can reach the 18–20 mph range.

Sources indicate that that higher speed comes from the bike’s Sport mode, which became my default setting. It requires a bit more pedaling to reach full assist, which explains why my smartwatch recorded my heart rate in the moderate-to-vigorous zone if I was riding above 20 mph.) The other modes are Eco (minimal assist, with you supplying most of the power), Turbo (max power with little effort, making uphill climbs trivial), and Auto (which adjusts assist level to your pedaling). You can also tune each setting to your liking.

The added bulk is also meant to handle rougher terrain. I’ve had the occasional flat tire from road debris on slimmer bikes, so I appreciate the sturdier, all-terrain, flat-resistant tires. Still, the 70-pound frame makes me hesitant to venture too far from pavement. I won’t be bombing down any mountain bike trails, but it’s helpful to have the option to jump off a curb or ride on dirt or gravel roads.

The weight makes the bike markedly different from the previous Turbo Vado we reviewed; this isn’t a bike I’d want to ride without assistance. Even the Eco mode, which you’d have to use exclusively to get the bike’s purported 150-km (93-mile), five-hour range, felt a bit sluggish compared to the more powerful modes I preferred. Specialized also sells a 280-Whr range extender, but at $700, it feels like overkill.

It has been revealed that the RockShox Psylo suspension fork, with 120 mm of travel, also made this the smoothest-riding e-bike I’ve tested. Other e-bikes I’ve ridden have felt stiff over even small bumps in the road, but the Evo’s bounciness made hitting bumps feel like a nice change of pace. I used to be scared of going over a curb, and that’s no longer the case. The 40 mm dropper seatpost is another nice feature, giving riders a bit of travel and letting them lower the seat to make it easier to touch the ground when stopped or dismounting.

Credit: Specialized Credit: Specialized.

While other e-bikes I’ve owned initially offered good range, storing them in colder weather has been an problem for their longevity.

So I’m grateful that Specialized made the downtube battery removable. Being able to store the battery in my house helps since I keep my bikes in an outdoor shed—I no longer have to worry about it sitting in freezing temperatures. A full charge takes four hours, though you can tweak the battery to cap charging at 80 percent to further extend its life.

Industry observers note that the other electric components are nice, too. On the Evo 5.0 I rode, a touchscreen lets you cycle through ride data, including your speed, estimated range remaining, and power assistance level. The front light even comes with low-beam (450 lumens) and high-beam (805 lumens) settings, making my night rides more visible.

If I have any complaints about my time with this bike, they boil down to two things. First, it’s incredibly heavy, making it difficult for many people to take up stairs. Second, the convenience of riding at high speed and making quick journeys has left my road bike gathering dust unless I’m specifically going out for a workout (and those are harder now that I’m so accustomed to riding the Evo). That’s more of a personal concern than a mark against the bike, though. It’s fun to ride, but maybe at the cost of consistent manual pedaling.

Sources indicate that and then there’s the cost. I tested the Evo 5.0 ($5,200), which sits between the 4.0 ($4,500) and 6.0 ($7,000) in terms of cost, performance, and features. At $5,200, though, I would’ve liked to see a phone mount on the 5.0, which is a common enough feature on less-expensive bikes.

Those prices make securing the bike even more key, and Specialized offers a few safety features to thwart theft. As mentioned, you can remove the battery, lock the back wheel, and disable the power system; there’s also Apple Find My integration if the bike ever escapes your purview (a bummer if you use Android, though).

It has been revealed that in all, Specialized has upgraded the e-bike experience enough for me to want to upgrade, though the price makes me blanch a bit. Maybe I can subsidize a purchase by selling an older e-bike.

  • With this change, the Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes cost of a large server no longer grows with its vCPU count.

Sources indicate that amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) Hybrid Nodes now has lower pricing for large nodes, capping the billed vCPU per node at 32 vCPU, so you are no longer charged for vCPUs above that per node threshold. Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes lets you use your existing on-premises and edge infrastructure as nodes in Amazon EKS clusters. You can now use your largest servers, including those with GPUs, with Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes at lower cost.

With this change, the Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes cost of a large server no longer grows with its vCPU count. At the first pricing tier, a 64 vCPU node now costs 50% less than before, and a 256 vCPU node costs 88% less, as both are now billed only for 32 vCPUs. This makes Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes more cost-effective for large bare-metal and GPU servers running compute-intensive workloads, such as AI/ML training and inference, that must stay on-premises for data residency, latency, or regulatory reasons. The pricing change applies automatically to all latest hybrid nodes. For the new pricing to take effect for existing hybrid nodes attached to clusters, delete and reattach them. Nodes with 32 vCPUs or fewer are still billed for their actual vCPUs, and existing tiered pricing still applies, so your effective rate falls as monthly usage grows.

Sources indicate that the new pricing is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes is available. To learn more about getting started and updated pricing details, visit the Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes documentation and Amazon EKS pricing page.

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (241 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Amazon

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Starting today, Amazon RDS for MySQL supports MySQL major version 9.7, the latest Long-Term Support release from MySQL community.
  • Industry observers note that the Replication Applier Metrics help you diagnose replication lag by adding two Performance Schema tables that report per-channel applier backlog, throughput, and wait statistics, along with each worker's progress on its current transaction.
  • Industry observers note that you can upgrade your database using Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments, in-place upgrade, or restore from a snapshot.

Starting today, Amazon RDS for MySQL supports MySQL major version 9.7, the latest Long-Term Support release from MySQL community. Amazon RDS for MySQL 9.7 launches with community MySQL 9.7.4. This launch introduces support for the Replication Applier Metrics component, JSON Duality Views, and Hypergraph Optimizer.

Industry observers note that the Replication Applier Metrics help you diagnose replication lag by adding two Performance Schema tables that report per-channel applier backlog, throughput, and wait statistics, along with each worker's progress on its current transaction. JSON Duality Views let applications read and write the same relational tables as JSON documents. The Hypergraph Optimizer is an opt-in query optimizer that can improve execution prepares for complex, multi-join queries. For more details, refer to the MySQL 9.7.4 release notes and the Amazon RDS for MySQL release notes.

Industry observers note that you can upgrade your database using Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments, in-place upgrade, or restore from a snapshot. #7471. Industry News: The "shameful" measles data that lost the US its elimination status

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1672 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: The "shameful" measles data that lost the US its elimination status

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1672 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that international health authorities formally announced on Tuesday that the US has lost its measles elimination status, a hard-fought public health triumph won in 2000 after decades-long vaccination efforts.
  • Sources indicate that after the announcement Tuesday, public health experts, doctors, and political leaders decried the dramatic backslide for the US, calling it “shameful” and a “national embarrassment.” News articles point to the staggering vertical rise of measles cases this year, currently over 5,400 cases, more than any other year since 1991.
  • According to recent reports, but the measles data that caused the US to lose its status—the bits of it that are public at least—paint a darker picture of where the US is in its rematch with measles, the most contagious virus known on Earth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that international health authorities formally announced on Tuesday that the US has lost its measles elimination status, a hard-fought public health triumph won in 2000 after decades-long vaccination efforts. The loss had been widely expected by public health experts for months, and the decision was leaked by the press last week. Still, having the designation officially stripped stings.

Sources indicate that after the announcement Tuesday, public health experts, doctors, and political leaders decried the dramatic backslide for the US, calling it “shameful” and a “national embarrassment.” News articles point to the staggering vertical rise of measles cases this year, currently over 5,400 cases, more than any other year since 1991. An explosive measles outbreak in Pennsylvania accounts for over 1,500 of those cases. There have been 10 confirmed deaths across three states, several deaths just in the last week.

According to recent reports, but the measles data that caused the US to lose its status—the bits of it that are public at least—paint a darker picture of where the US is in its rematch with measles, the most contagious virus known on Earth. For one thing, almost none of the data from this year—the cases, the explosive Pennsylvania outbreak, the deaths—factored in to the loss. It was lost earlier. What’s happening now is a runaway epidemic.

The US measles elimination status is a designation granted by the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), which is a regional division of the World Health Organization. Last week a committee of experts assembled by the PAHO, called the RVC, met to review measles data for countries across the region, including the US. (RVC is short for the Measles, Rubella and Congenital Rubella Syndrome Elimination Regional Monitoring and Re-Verification Commission.).

For their review of the US data, the RVC heard from an independent committee of experts from the US, called the NSC, which presented measles data collected from January 2025 onward. (The NSC is short for the US National Sustainability Committee for the Elimination of Measles, Rubella, and Congenital Rubella Syndrome.).

It has been revealed that according to the PAHO, an elimination status is lost when epidemiological and laboratory data shows that a single viral lineage has spread continuously for at least 12 months within a country. At this point, the virus is considered to be reestablished or endemic. So, to withdraw the US elimination status, the RVC needed to see evidence that a single introduction of a measles virus led to a 12-month-long chain of cases, which requires a lot of data.

It has been revealed that the full set of data the NSC presented to the RVC is private for now. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention needs to review and approve such data for public release, which can be a lengthy process that has not yet occurred.

The Department of Health and Human Services, which oversees the CDC, did not respond to a question from Ars Technica regarding when the data may be released.

But Ars Technica spoke with the chair of the NSC, Noel Brewer, who tried to talk through the pieces of data in the NSC report to the PAHO that he could discuss—these are pieces that have already been made public at some point by others, such as by state health officials or researchers. Brewer remarked the NSC presented the PAHO with genetic data spanning January 2025 to January 2026, and also epidemiological data that extended to June 2026.

In a press briefing Tuesday, officials for the PAHO made clear that only some of the data presented by NSC factored into its assessment of the US elimination status. The RVC only looked at the reporting period between January 2025 and January 2026, which doesn’t include the massive outbreak ongoing in Pennsylvania, which began in April. “The number of cases in Pennsylvania did not actually contribute to the decision that was made by the Reverification Commission,” Rhonda Sealey-Thomas, PAHO’s assistant director, explicitly told reporters Tuesday. For 2025, the US reported 2,289 cases nationally.

Still, there was no ambiguity about the US losing its status; “multiple lines of data show clearly that the US has sustained transmission of measles,” Brewer told Ars.

Brewer, who is also the Gillings Distinguished Professor in Public Health at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, confirmed that the beginning of the end of US elimination was January 20, 2025, in Texas—that date was included in the letter PAHO sent to the US informing it of the loss of elimination status. That Texas outbreak was declared over on August 18, 2025, after 762 cases were confirmed in the state. But the virus carried on elsewhere and is still simmering.

“Since January 20, 2025, the US, Canada, and Mexico have been passing measles cases back and forth across borders,” Brewer noted, and the national data highlights multiple, “genetically distinct” measles introductions into the US. “However, there is one genomic lineage that predominates across the cases and ties many of them, the majority of them, together,” he said.

Sources indicate that for people closely tracking the US measles status, a key question has been whether the massive outbreaks that followed the initial one in Texas were clearly linked. If they were, it would be immediately obvious that the US had lost the elimination status; but if not, and the outbreaks were driven by different virus introductions, the US could have kept its measles-free status based on the technicality of how the status is defined.

Data that might hold the answer to this question has been elusive. The measles strain in Texas, D8-9171, appeared similar to the viruses seen subsequently in substantial outbreaks in Arizona and Utah. But the strain was also similar to those from Mexico and Canada. Generally, there can be relatively small genetic changes among measles viruses, and genetic data alone is not used by PAHO to evaluate elimination. In June, ProPublica tried to get at the answer itself, conducting its own genetic analysis of measles strains in the US. It concluded that “the measles virus still spreading in Utah as of this May is very closely related to the one that sickened Texans over a year ago.” But the outlet acknowledged this wasn’t a “smoking gun.”.

According to recent reports, to date, the question lingers. Brewer cannot yet explicitly disclose what the NSC reported to the PAHO about possible links between the Texas outbreak and any of the subsequent large outbreaks in 2025. That includes the one in nearby Utah or one in South Carolina, which began in October 2025 and ultimately tallied 997 cases by the time it was declared over in April 2026.

For its part, the PAHO did not respond to multiple requests for comment from Ars Technica on linkages between the outbreaks.

But in a twist, Brewer noted that the answer to the question might be moot; the lineage that started in Texas on January 20 might not be the only one that has been sustained and could have lost the country its status. There are “one or two that have gone on for more than 12 months,” he stated.

It has been revealed that with the designation now formally lost, health and medical experts are coming to grips with the reality that measles is once again endemic in the US. Details of how the US should move forward are up for debate; the US is now required to submit a “corrective action proposal” to the PAHO, outlining how the country intends to regain its elimination status. But the fundamental solution is obvious and straightforward: The US needs to increase vaccination rates.

Sources indicate that while the virus has been raging in religious communities with low vaccination rates, the entire US has seen slipping vaccination coverage. That makes it easier for the virus to gain a foothold virtually anywhere.

A protective vaccination rate is considered to be 95 percent; according to the latest data, only 92.4 percent of kindergartners were vaccinated with the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine in the 2025–2026 school year. Only 10 states have MMR vaccination rates at or above the 95 percent threshold. Meanwhile, non-medical exemptions from school vaccination requirements have never been higher, at 4 percent. Presently, 24 states have exemption rates at or above 5 percent, meaning that even if they are able to vaccinate every single non-exempt child, they would still not meet the 95 percent target. And this is just the data for young children. The vaccination coverage for adults is another concern, and the data there is scarce. In Pennsylvania’s massive outbreak, 1,055 of the 1,561 cases this year have been in adults ages 18 and older (less than 1 percent of the cases were fully vaccinated).

While some health officials have noted optimistically that 92.4 percent in children is just a few percentage points from the target, the reality of bringing up vaccination rates is more onerous.

PAHO Director Jarbas Barbosa stressed the point in the press briefing Tuesday: It’s “not the national average or the average in the state or even the average in a big city, you need to guarantee that in every community, village, you have this vaccination coverage up to 95 percent. This is very key,” Barbosa mentioned.

The point has been demonstrated in the US. In 2019, the US came very close to losing its measles elimination status. Unlike now—when the virus is on a nationwide rampage, with 47 states and jurisdictions reporting cases—in 2019, the US nearly lost its status from a single, large outbreak that spread in Latest York. Though it didn’t explode on a national level, it took 11 months to stamp out in those undervaccinated communities. In that year, the US reported 1,274 measles cases total.

Recent findings suggest that the situation in the US has only gotten worse, and the outlook is bleak, Brewer warns. “The measles outbreaks in Canada and Mexico are winding down,” he noted. “However, in the US, our measles problem continues to accelerate. There is no end in sight.”.

Amazon Cognito now supports point-in-time recovery

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (237 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Amazon

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that amazon Cognito now supports point-in-time recovery (PITR), so you can restore the user data in a user pool to an earlier time.
  • Industry observers note that with PITR, you choose a recovery point, preview how many customers, groups, multi-factor authentication (MFA) settings, and passkeys the recovery will create, revision, or delete, and then start or cancel the recovery.
  • Sources indicate that PITR is enabled automatically for user pools on the Essentials and Plus feature aims at no additional charge.

It has been revealed that amazon Cognito now supports point-in-time recovery (PITR), so you can restore the user data in a user pool to an earlier time. Amazon Cognito helps you implement secure sign-in and access control for consumers, AI agents, and microservices. Previously, you had to build and maintain your own export and restore process, and restored users received upcoming identifiers and had to reset their passwords.

Industry observers note that with PITR, you choose a recovery point, preview how many customers, groups, multi-factor authentication (MFA) settings, and passkeys the recovery will create, revision, or delete, and then start or cancel the recovery. Recovered users keep their identifiers, passwords, MFA settings, and passkeys, so they can sign in without resetting their credentials. For example, if a script deletes or modifies users by mistake, you can restore the user data to the moment before it ran.

Sources indicate that PITR is enabled automatically for user pools on the Essentials and Plus feature aims at no additional charge. The recovery window is up to 1 day on Essentials and up to 14 days on Plus. You can initiate and manage a recovery using the AWS Management Console, the Amazon Cognito API, AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), or AWS SDKs. PITR is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Cognito is available. To learn more, see Point-in-time recovery in the Amazon Cognito Developer Guide.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that I squint my eyes in confusion when Anton Osika asks if I like cakes. The CEO of Lovable was in the middle of explaining how his AI startup, flush with investment cash and recently valued at over $13 billion, is ready to shift its focus after two years. Why does the vibe-coding king care if I like sweet treats? He thinks that if I do, I might be able to vibe code a living out of that.

The generative AI revolution completely flipped coding. Rather than a niche skill set where humans had to learn how to talk like computers, software development could be done by computers generating code in response to natural-language requests from humans.

Sources indicate that osika was early to this shift, launching a viral open-source tool in 2023, a precursor to Lovable. His mission? “Reduce barriers to build.” That initial spark ignited what is now one of Europe’s most dynamic startups.

Tech insiders talked nonstop last year about the transformative power of “vibe coding” that could empower anyone to build their own software. Parents could whip up custom apps to help track demanding club sports schedules. Picky eaters could create dynamic meal plans that adapt to whatever’s in their fridge. Polyamorous people could build software to manage their relationship hierarchies. Whatever random, niche software you can imagine, you can build it.

According to recent reports, but Osika isn’t satisfied with helping millions of people vibe code apps for their everyday life—he also wants Lovable people to make more cash. The startup claims that around 80 percent of users arrive at the platform with a financial incentive, like building customer-facing platforms for online sales. That said, Lovable also reports that only 35 percent right now earn revenue with their projects.

That brings us back to the cake question. Lovable’s initiative for next year is to help you run a small business based on your passions, like opening a cake shop. Fabian Hedin, Lovable’s other cofounder and chief technology officer, says the startup is building automations to help with everything from initial business strategy and website creation to long-term customer retention and marketing intends.

For example, a cake shop owner receives an AI-generated morning briefing through a chatbot-style, Lovable dashboard. “You set some goals, and then the AI is proactive in helping you reach those goals,” Hedin says. This briefing analyzes the number of cake boxes sold through a holiday promotion, customer emails it automatically answered, and reminders to make financial deposits on time.

It has been revealed that lovable has been a boon for savvy social media content creators, who can leverage their platforms better through vibe-coded sites. “People who have audiences themselves are building larger businesses around that,” Osika states. He recently went to a dinner in Upcoming York with creators, one of whom uses Lovable to help sell their book. Others have used it to help hawk merch.

Recent findings suggest that lovable earning the trust of burgeoning entrepreneurs is critical to the success of this new endeavor, though it may be an uphill battle. Vibe-coded projects were notorious for not necessarily being secure and sometimes exposing user data.

The startup was one of many vibe-coded services that came under fire this year for facilitating user-generated apps that exposed data on the open web. Earlier this month, Lovable revamped its security approach as part of its effort to make sites generated through its platform more secure by default.

Sources indicate that “The moment real people use what you build, security is the product,” Igor Andriushchenko, Lovable’s head of security, tells WIRED. “That's why it's one of the areas we continue investing in the most and why we’ve built it directly into the platform experience.”.

Sources indicate that osika will see Lovable as successful next year if he can help a new wave of entrepreneurs start sustainable businesses. Why just vibe code an app when you can vibe code a living?

When I first sat down with Ben and Asher Spector to discuss Flapping Airplanes, I felt both of these to be true at once.

Asher, one year Benâs senior, is a former debate champion turned Stanford statistics Ph.D. The brothers have an eye for raw talent, and aged 25 and 26 respectively, they are building the âyoung personâs AGI lab.â Their co-founder Aidan Smith is a former founder and Thiel fellow who worked at Neuralink for three years while in college at Georgia Tech. Ben and Asher believe that raw talent â the type of people who would previously have gone on to do Ph.D.s or join quant firms â are the key to unlocking the next phase of AI development. This stands in sharp contrast to the approach of focusing on âbrand nameâ AI talent at any price, which seems so in vogue right now.

There is something else that is countercultural about this lab too: they recognize that scale alone is not enough. Indeed, the lab is predicated on this notion. There is only one Internet, and weâve run out of it. Data is the bottleneck today to further AI scaling, not compute. Todayâs AI models are wildly inefficient, something that Dwarkesh Patel has recently hammered home in his interviews with Andrej Karpathy, Richard Sutton and others. Flapping Airplanes is dedicated to searching for a more data-efficient AI. The companyâs name is a nod to a more biological notion of machine intelligence.

One of the fundamental debates right now in AI is around scaling vs. research. The scaling paradigm argues for dedicating a huge amount of societyâs resources, as much as the economy can muster, toward scaling up todayâs LLMs, in the hopes that this will lead to AGI. The research paradigm argues that we are 2-3 research breakthroughs away from an âAGIâ intelligence, and as a result, we should dedicate resources to long-running research, especially projects that may take 5-10 years to come to fruition.

In a recent development, while the divide between these two schools of thought is far from absolute â research breakthroughs make compute investments more efficient, and GPUs are required for net fresh research â they each lead to different tradeoffs. A compute-first approach would prioritize cluster scale above all else, and would heavily favor short-term wins (on the order of 1-2 years) over long-term bets (on the order of 5-10 years). A research-first approach would spread bets temporally, and should be willing to make lots of bets that have a low absolute probability of working, but that collectively expand the search space for what is possible.

It has been revealed that one concern I have had is that by starving Ph.D. programs of talent, and by reallocating a lot of this talent to scale-oriented work (as opposed to fundamental research), we could actually push out the AGI timeline. As I noted in a previous blog post, âcorporate politics tends to favor in vogue, consensus ideas over more radical, unpopular ones â the very kinds of ideas that can take years to prove worthwhile, and which scientific breakthroughs often depend on.â Flapping Airplanes is explicitly intended to provide a Ph.D.-like experience â true research independence, long-time horizons â while bridging the pay gap between academia and Big Tech.

Industry observers note that one of the biggest learnings of the last decade in AI is the dramatic economic value of fundamental scientific progress. And they are focused on precisely the problem that is likely to define the next wave of AI: building models inspired by the data efficiency of biology. With that as a north star, the company will make bets in a variety of directions to get there.

Recent findings suggest that there are two coherent motives right now in AI. One is the profit motive, and this should inspire all application builders, given the tremendous opportunity ahead. As I have noted on many occasions, AI is so underpenetrated relative to the capability set available, it is likely to create a golden age for builders for many years to come. There is a large profit pool available, and we are in the very earliest stages of generating it.

Industry observers note that the second coherent motive in AI is AGI, predicated on the belief that now that weâve unlocked a machine intelligence, we should push toward upleveling that intelligence. Economically, progress in this direction is likely to be extremely valuable. The question is how to take on this objective in an efficient way, with a reasonable probability that resources invested will translate into long-term positive results. Trump admin orders Kalshi to halt wagers on what words Trump will say

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the Trump administration ordered prediction market Kalshi to stop offering event contracts that pay out based on whether President Trump will say a specific word before a particular date.
  • CNBC reported yesterday that “Kalshi quietly paused trading in a handful of ‘mention’ contracts tied to President Donald Trump at the end of last week at the request of the CFTC.” Kalshi told media outlets that it is complying with the CFTC order.
  • It has been revealed that the markets taken down by Kalshi allowed users to wager on whether Trump would say certain words, including nicknames and the names of countries and companies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Trump administration ordered prediction market Kalshi to stop offering event contracts that pay out based on whether President Trump will say a specific word before a particular date. Kalshi halted trading in the contracts while the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) conducts a review into whether the Trump mention contracts violate federal law.

CNBC reported yesterday that “Kalshi quietly paused trading in a handful of ‘mention’ contracts tied to President Donald Trump at the end of last week at the request of the CFTC.” Kalshi told media outlets that it is complying with the CFTC order.

It has been revealed that the markets taken down by Kalshi allowed users to wager on whether Trump would say certain words, including nicknames and the names of countries and companies. A similar expired event contract that can still be viewed on Kalshi’s website asked whether Trump would use the nicknames “Marjorie Traitor Greene,” “Sleepy Joe,” and “Whack Job” or “Wack Job” before April 2026.

The CFTC order issued to Kalshi last week applies broadly to “the TRUMPSAY contract series.” The event contracts in this series include trades in the format, “Will [word] be noted by Donald Trump after Issuance and before [date]?” The CFTC order also applied to a specific event contract that asks, “What nicknames will Trump say before 2027?”.

The CFTC order came several months after the federal agency settled charges against a Trump teleprompter aide who made over $100,000 in Kalshi wagers on what Trump would say in prepared remarks. On August 28, the CFTC required the man, Gabriel Perez, to disgorge profits of $107,539.02 and pay a civil penalty of $65,000.

“In his position, Perez had access to presidential speeches prior to those speeches being delivered and Perez misappropriated that information—in breach of his duty of trust and confidence—to trade presidential mention market contracts, generating over $107,500 in profits,” the CFTC mentioned at the time.

According to recent reports, senate Democrats recently said the White House hasn’t taken meaningful action against insider trading, “all while the president and his family stand to personally profit from their participation in prediction markets.” Prediction markets have flourished under the Trump administration’s permissive regulatory approach. The CFTC has allowed prediction markets to offer sports gambling nationwide and filed lawsuits against states that attempt to regulate Kalshi under their gambling laws.

It has been revealed that kalshi recently dropped Donald Trump Jr. as an advisor, saying it made the decision because Trump Jr.’s venture capital firm increased its investment in its competitor, Polymarket. Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour also acknowledged that the “optics” of Trump Jr.’s advisory role weren’t good for Kalshi. Trump Jr. still stands to benefit from Kalshi’s success, because he was given equity shares in the organization.

The CFTC has remarked that mention markets are easily manipulated but reviews them on a case-by-case basis instead of prohibiting them. Prediction markets can “self-certify” that any latest event contract complies with US law and start offering it without waiting for the CFTC’s permission, but the CFTC can halt trading afterward based on reviews of specific contracts.

Recent findings suggest that the Commodity Exchange Act (CEA) prohibits the listing of contracts that are readily susceptible to manipulation. CFTC staff issued a September advisory about the legality of markets on what people will say, and whether they will attend an event or interact with another person. The advisory said these contracts may be viewed as “presumptively readily susceptible to manipulation,” because they “may be controlled by a single individual, a small group of individuals, or persons with access to or influence over the individual whose words, attendance, or interaction determines settlement.”.

The CFTC mentioned this type of contract requires measures “to prevent manipulation and misappropriation of material non-public information,” and that Kalshi failed to comply with the CFTC staff advisory. About “a week after the Staff Advisory was released, Kalshi listed the Contract [on nicknames] for trading without amending the [TRUMPSAY] Contract Series’ self-certification (or submitting a upcoming self-certification) to make the ‘heightened showing’ of non-manipulability required by the Staff Advisory,” the order said.

The CFTC said it will conduct “a proceeding to determine whether the certification of the Contracts was false—that is, whether the Contracts comply with the Act, including the Core Principles, and Commission regulations thereunder as Kalshi has certified.” So far, “Kalshi has not adequately demonstrated that the Contracts are not readily susceptible to manipulation” as required by law, the order said.

“Given the available supporting evidence, including that Kalshi has not attempted to establish that the Contracts are non-manipulable with respect to the Staff Advisory’s guidance, the Commission presumptively believes the certification is false,” the order said.

The CFTC order is not a determination on whether the Trump mention markets can meet the standard of not being readily susceptible to manipulation. Rather, it is a determination that Kalshi has so far failed to show that the contracts are not easily manipulated.

The order “resolves only that, based on the current record, Kalshi has not demonstrated that the Contracts as certified comply with the Act and that the Contracts should not trade while the Commission completes its review,” the CFTC noted.

We contacted Kalshi and will upgrade this article if it provides a response.

Mansour defended the Trump mention contracts at an Axios event on Tuesday, according to Bloomberg. “What the president does say moves markets,” Mansour said. “So predicting what he’s about to say is actually pretty meaningful.”.

The Bloomberg article noted that “Kalshi’s main rival Polymarket still has live mention markets tied to Trump’s speeches on its international website, which is not regulated by the CFTC.” Polymarket offers a separate US-regulated version of its prediction market.

Best Buy is selling Blu-rays directly through its website and in physical stores again after exiting Blu-ray and DVD sales in 2023.

The Best Buy website’s movie section at the moment lists 15 Blu-rays (including one two-pack) that are “sold & shipped by Best Buy.” Fresh titles available include The Odyssey (2026), Project Hail Mary (2026), Supergirl (2026), Super Mario Galaxy (2026), and Obsession (2025). Best Buy is also selling some older titles on Blu-ray, including It’s a Wonderful Life (1943), Saving Private Ryan (1998), and The Godfather (1972).

Industry observers note that most of the Blu-rays are available for purchase online and can be delivered to an address or picked up at a Best Buy store within a few days. As of this writing, The Odyssey appears to be in stock at Best Buy stores, as it’s currently listed as available for pickup within as little as an hour.

Ars Technica reached out to Best Buy to ask whether customers can expect the store to continue selling Blu-rays moving forward.

In October 2023, Best Buy announced that it would stop selling Blu-rays and DVDs online and in stores starting in 2024.

According to recent reports, “To state the obvious, the way we watch movies and TV reveals is much different today than it was decades ago. Making this change gives us more space and opportunity to bring customers new and innovative tech for them to explore, discover and enjoy,” a Best Buy spokesperson mentioned in a statement issued at the time.

Last year, the Best Buy website started selling Blu-rays and DVDs from third parties via its online marketplace.

In a recent development, numerous other companies have reduced or ended their Blu-ray and/or DVD businesses in recent years. Target, for instance, only sells the discs in stores during special occasions (like holidays or for significant releases) now. Disney outsourced its DVD and Blu-ray business to Sony, which subsequently stopped selling recordable Blu-rays to people, and DVD rental company Redbox went out of business.

It has been revealed that that said, physical media, including Blu-rays and DVDs, still have a place in many people’s homes. Because digital copies of movies and indicates can be plucked from online platforms and people’s libraries that were previously “purchased” (but truly only rented) without warning, enthusiasts continue relying on physical media. Enthusiasts also opt for physical copies of movies and shows for better picture and/or sound quality than what’s available digitally, as well as for bragging rights.

According to recent reports, overall, the sales of Blu-rays and DVDs in the US have been steadily declining, and annual consumer spending dropped 9.3 percent from 2024 to 2025, according to the Digital Entertainment Group (DEG). During this same time, however, consumer spending on 4K Blu-ray discs specifically increased 12 percent year over year, per DEG.

A resurgence in Blu-ray sales has been associated with the growth of collectible SteelBooks, which are Blu-rays sold in collectible steel boxes, and Gen Z, which, in some cases, are even turning to video rental stores for Blu-rays and DVDs.

Industry observers note that “We’re seeing a lot of evidence, including at the Criterion Mobile Closet, that more young people are thinking about physical media in a different way,” Peter Becker, president of Criterion, which sells Blu-rays and DVDs online, told the Los Angeles Times in February. “In an age where so much is available to us on demand, it becomes increasingly crucial to us.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that AWS Lambda now supports GPU-accelerated Event Functions on Lambda Managed Instances using EC2 G-series instances.
  • Running GPU workloads today requires customers to provision hardware, manage driver and framework dependencies, and build custom scaling and capacity management.
  • According to recent reports, GPU-accelerated Event Functions on Lambda Managed Instances is available in all AWS Commercial Regions where Lambda Managed Instances and EC2 G-series instances are available.

It has been revealed that AWS Lambda now supports GPU-accelerated Event Functions on Lambda Managed Instances using EC2 G-series instances. You can now run GPU-accelerated workloads including AI inference, media processing, 3D rendering, scientific computing, and financial simulations on Lambda without managing GPU drivers, frameworks, or scaling. Lambda runs multiple invocations concurrently in each execution environment and scales responsively based on GPU utilization, CPU utilization, and concurrency to keep your GPUs busy and reduce costs. GPU-accelerated functions integrate with the same 200+ AWS event sources as other Event Functions, so you can add GPU compute as another step in your serverless application.

Running GPU workloads today requires customers to provision hardware, manage driver and framework dependencies, and build custom scaling and capacity management. With this launch, you can go from code to a running GPU workload in minutes. Lambda provides GPU base images preconfigured with frameworks such as vLLM, SGLang, and PyTorch. You can run workloads with large artifacts using container images and NVMe ephemeral storage of up to 32 GB each. To reduce startup time, Lambda supports Seekable OCI (SOCI) lazy loading and streaming artifacts directly from Amazon S3. For resilience, you can select G-series instance types from multiple generations in the allowed instance types for your capacity provider. Lambda provisions instances from the newest generation that meets your function requirements and falls back to older generations when capacity is unavailable.

According to recent reports, GPU-accelerated Event Functions on Lambda Managed Instances is available in all AWS Commercial Regions where Lambda Managed Instances and EC2 G-series instances are available. You can configure GPU-accelerated functions using the AWS Console, AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, AWS CloudFormation, AWS CDK, or AWS SAM. You can also use this feature through coding assistants such as Kiro, Claude Code, or Codex by installing the Lambda Managed Instances skill from the Agent Toolkit for AWS. You pay the EC2 On-Demand price (Savings Prepares and Reserved Instances apply) for your instance, plus a 9.75% Lambda management fee and $0.20 per million requests. To learn more, visit the AWS Lambda Developer Guide and AWS Lambda Pricing.

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

Windows Server 2028 trades compatibility for out-of-the-box security

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (576 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that microsoft’s Ignite announcements this week went beyond the Office-in-Copilot overhaul with the reveal of the Windows Server 2028 Public Preview and its upcoming security-by-default stance and what Microsoft calls Hardened Server Core.
  • Recent findings suggest that STIGs work by providing a standard security framework for system administrators to follow recommended guidance.
  • The upcoming Windows Server 2028 hardened-by-default state will only be available for the Server Core installs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that microsoft’s Ignite announcements this week went beyond the Office-in-Copilot overhaul with the reveal of the Windows Server 2028 Public Preview and its upcoming security-by-default stance and what Microsoft calls Hardened Server Core. Windows Server 2028 will implement a default security framework that Microsoft says is aligned with hardened DoD benchmarks, such as the Defense Information Systems Agency’s (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG).

Recent findings suggest that STIGs work by providing a standard security framework for system administrators to follow recommended guidance. In the past, Windows Server admins were left to start from a blank canvas and then implement hardening configurations for operations. Secure baselines were available but not the default. Microsoft states that concern is now managed: “The secure configuration is the starting state, not a project you run after setup. That closes the window where a newly deployed server sits exposed while it waits to be hardened.”.

The upcoming Windows Server 2028 hardened-by-default state will only be available for the Server Core installs. Windows Server Desktop Experience installs do not include the changed stance.

Industry observers note that this isn’t to say that system administrators won’t still have the final say on which security protocols are activated, just that the default package now ships in a pre-hardened state. Kerberos is now the default over NTLM, with protections added to LSASS; TLS is automatically restricted to modern cipher suites; key exchange uses “hybrid post-quantum key exchange” based on the quantum-safe ML-KEM; and remote desktop authentication and PowerShell script block logging get stricter as well.

Microsoft’s native NVMe storage stack was originally introduced via an enhancement to Windows Server 2025, but it required administrators to enable it manually. The update eliminated NVMe translation through a SCSI stack while improving speeds and reducing overhead. The redesigned stack will now be default-on in Windows Server 2028.

Sources indicate that microsoft is upfront, noting that the newly introduced hardened security settings may break things due to software compatibility issues with older protocols, legacy authentication, or management tools and scripts. The organization encourages owners to try things and provide feedback about what goes wrong. “We want to hear where a hardened default gets in the way of a real workload: which setting, which application, and what you had to change to get it working,” the Windows Server Team said in a blog post. “That is how the defaults get better before general availability.”.

According to recent reports, microsoft suggests that consumers use the preview build as a test bed to determine where challenges like compatibility still arise. This is not a release candidate build and shouldn’t be treated as such. Despite the new security stance that comes with the preview build, hardware-backed protections like Secure Boot and DMA requirements won’t be enforced until a later preview build. Kerberos is now the default preference over NTLM, but NTLM blocking itself will still have to wait for a later preview release.

Beyond those limitations, the current build has a known glitch that cuts into its hardened goals. According to the release notes, “A race condition in the TLS hybrid key exchange implementation may cause the LSASS service to crash when hybrid groups are negotiated by a TLS server.” Microsoft recommends disabling hybrid-key exchange groups until the problem is addressed.

System administrators and curious homelabbers interested in testing the fresh Windows Server 2028 can do so by registering with the Microsoft Windows Insider Program.

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (190 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Amazon

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Amazon CloudFront (CF) now supports WebSocket and gRPC traffic to application origins in AWS regions, with mutual TLS authentication between CF and the application origin (origin mTLS).
  • Previously, customers serving WebSocket or gRPC traffic through CloudFront had to use shared secrets or IP allow-lists to identify requests originating from CloudFront.
  • Sources indicate that there is no additional charge for origin mTLS, and it is available with pay-as-you-go pricing and in the Business and Premium flat-rate pricing plans.

Amazon CloudFront (CF) now supports WebSocket and gRPC traffic to application origins in AWS regions, with mutual TLS authentication between CF and the application origin (origin mTLS). Customers can now use TLS certificates to authenticate requests from CloudFront while setting up WebSocket or gRPC connections to their origins. Origin mTLS protects internet facing applications that need persistent, bidirectional or streaming connections, such as chat platforms, collaborative editing tools or live dashboards from unauthenticated requests.

Previously, customers serving WebSocket or gRPC traffic through CloudFront had to use shared secrets or IP allow-lists to identify requests originating from CloudFront. This was operationally complex and did not provide strong authentication. With Origin mTLS, customers can use one TLS based authentication for HTTP, WebSocket and gRPC traffic to an application origin. This works with application origins within AWS such as Application Load Balancer and API Gateway, on-premises origins, and origins hosted outside AWS.

Sources indicate that there is no additional charge for origin mTLS, and it is available with pay-as-you-go pricing and in the Business and Premium flat-rate pricing plans. To learn more, visit the CloudFront origin mutual TLS documentation.

While they may not be able to levitate or act like a Jetsons-style robot personal assistant (yet), smart beds these days come pretty close to accomplishing both. Like adjustable mattresses, smart beds offer modifiable firmness and the ability to raise and lower the head and foot. These days, though, smart beds offer so much more, integrating features like dual-climate control, sleep tracking, and massage therapies.

Recent findings suggest that the best smart bed is, by far, the Bryte Balance Pro Smart Mattress, and if you’re looking for the most luxurious, it’s the Tempur-Pedic Tempur-ActiveBreeze. Let me break it down for you below.

For more old-school mattresses, check out our guides to the Best Mattresses, the Best Organic Mattresses, and the Best Mattresses for Back Pain.

In a recent development, updated November 2026: I’ve updated product information and the FAQ section. Discontinued products were removed, and I updated specs, prices, and links.

I’m at the moment testing the Eight Sleep Pod 6.

Recent findings suggest that most smart beds on the market use air chambers on each side of the mattress to achieve adjustable firmness. This is fine, but you can definitely feel them beneath you. But that's not the case with Bryte's Balance Pro, which is why it's so great.

Instead of air chambers, this smart bed is designed with coils (Bryte Balancers) and memory foam layers. These coils can be adjusted to specific zones, and if you want extra lumbar support or contouring, you can customize each section through the companion app. There are also 100 firmness levels, which makes it suitable for a variety of sleepers, from belly sleepers to larger-bodied individuals who may find air-chambered beds too soft.

Former WIRED reviewer Julia Forbes’ favorite feature is the massage function, which gently presses the coils against you. The smart bed is controlled exclusively via app, where you can also view your sleep insights. Along with metrics like sleep stages, duration, and heart rate, it also tracks the number of bed rebalances, which is how many times the Bryte Balancers are auto-adjusted throughout the night. There’s also an AI Sleep Concierge that is best for getting tips on how to sleep better.

Bryte Balance Pro ranges from $5,999 for a twin mattress to $6,899 for a California king.

Hot sleepers and overheaters will love Tempur-Pedic's Tempur-ActiveBreeze. There are fans built into the adjustable base that disperse cool or warm air, with three airflow speeds (slow, medium, and fast). The airflow is streamlined from the base through two ports in the bed, and the perforated memory foam layers and coils help promote circulation. According to the company, the dual climate control offers a 30-degree temperature range, which is the largest we’ve come across in testing. Former WIRED reviewer Julia Forbes could feel the air lightly skittering along the surface. On the bright side, even when she piled on her heaviest bedding, she didn’t run hot once.

Industry observers note that the Tempur-ActiveBreeze also offers sleep tracking, AI coaching, and a suite of relaxation programs that combine meditative soundscapes and massage therapy to lull you to sleep. Probably most notably, there’s an automatic snore response, which raises your head if it detects a breathing disturbance. The companion app breaks down your sleep data into digestible nightly, monthly, and annual reports.

The Tempur-ActiveBreeze (base included via Tempur-Pedic) ranges from $10,398 for a queen to $19,396 for a split California king.

Personal Comfort (The Rejuvenate).

Personal Comfort (Power-Flex 4 base).

According to recent reports, personal Comfort’s Rejuvenate is a solid adjustable mattress for side sleepers. It doesn’t offer any additional features or sleep-tracking capabilities, so it doesn’t truly qualify as a smart bed in my book.

Recent findings suggest that nevertheless, the Rejuvenate is a side-sleeper-friendly option because of its deep memory foam layers that contour to the body. If you want to sink in while still relying on the 45 firmness levels to ensure you're getting the support you need, this is it. Former WIRED reviewer Julia Forbes found a medium-firm 30 to be ideal for a healthy spine alignment when side sleeping.

What About Personal Comfort’s Adjustable Base?

Recent findings suggest that an adjustable base is available as an add-on and helpful if you opt for one of Personal Comfort’s specialty bed sizes, such as the Queen Flex-Head or King Flex-Head. It’s the only way to move the head and foot of the Rejuvenate, as well as implement adjustable lumbar support, pillow tilt, and massage features.

Julia tested the Power Flex 4. It provides a firmer feel right around the midsection, and its lumbar adjustment setting really amps up back support. She did find the massage features to be uncomfortable, though, describing them as “increasingly aggressive vibrations, akin to tectonic plates.”.

FYI, Personal Comfort often runs a bundle promotion.

Should I Use a Sleep Tracker With a Smart Bed?

Recent findings suggest that some smart beds offer contactless sleep tracking, which eliminates the need for an additional wearable. That remarked, they do carry some limitations. They’re generally not as accurate as contact-based trackers and can overestimate sleep stages and miscalculate duration. They often can’t track the same breadth of physiological measurements as smartwatches and smart rings do. And they can misattribute data from a partner or pet sharing the bed. But they’re convenient, especially if you dislike wearing trackers to bed.

Personally, I still sleep with my Apple Watch Series 12 and/or Oura Ring 5 to bed to compare. But, if I forget to wear either, my smart bed is auto-tracking my slumber in the background.

Do I Need an Adjustable Base to Go With My Smart Bed?

In a recent development, you are very likely going to want an adjustable base to go with your smart bed in order to enjoy everything your smart bed has to offer. This is especially true if you are purchasing one with the expectation of being able to move the top and bottom of the bed into different angles, like “TV watching” and “zero gravity” settings.

What’s the Difference Between an Adjustable Bed and a Smart Bed?

In a recent development, generally speaking, adjustable beds and smart beds are similar in that they both can raise or lower different sections of your mattress, with a remote control or companion app. Smart beds take it up a notch by incorporating additional features, such as sleep tracking, temperature control, and automated adjustments.

Can a Smart Bed Work for All Sleeping Positions?

According to recent reports, smart beds often come in adjustable firmness levels, and therefore can work for all sleeping positions. However, just like with any other mattress, the fabric technology is a huge deciding factor when it comes to comfort.

Industry observers note that for example, the Bryte Balance Pro is a much better choice for stomach sleepers or if you have a heavier body type. Coil support simply does not compare to even the firmest of inflated air chambers, which are usually what make smart beds' firmness levels “adjustable.” On the other hand, the Rejuvenate has a softer feel right off the bat because of its memory foam layers, making it ideal for side sleepers who need pressure relief.

Do I Need Wi-Fi Connectivity for My Smart Bed to Work?

Yes—if the power goes out, your smart bed will likely go offline. Smart beds are factored into smart home technology, meaning they rely on Wi-Fi for full functionality, especially to track sleep data and maintain the firmness level you've chosen.

What Does WIRED Do With the Mattresses After Testing Them?

It has been revealed that these smart beds were provided for free as media samples, and we either return them to the company or donate without personal benefit when testing is done. Most of these beds went to nurses, students, families in need, or those with medical conditions that were affecting their sleep.

Amazon CloudFront standard logging now supports CMCD and additional log fields

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (166 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Amazon

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Amazon CloudFront standard logging now supports additional access log fields that were previously available only in CloudFront real-time logs.
  • The new fields include the IP address of the CloudFront server that handled the request, identifiers that separate traffic on a primary distribution from traffic on a staging distribution, and a media quality confidence score.
  • These fields are available in all CloudFront edge locations, and standard logging pricing applies.

Amazon CloudFront standard logging now supports additional access log fields that were previously available only in CloudFront real-time logs. You can now include these fields in your standard logs and deliver them to Amazon S3, Amazon CloudWatch Logs, or Amazon Data Firehose, without setting up an additional data stream for real-time logs.

The new fields include the IP address of the CloudFront server that handled the request, identifiers that separate traffic on a primary distribution from traffic on a staging distribution, and a media quality confidence score. They also include Common Media Client Data (CMCD) fields, which video players send with each request to report details like bitrate, buffer length, and playback session ID. Streaming teams can use these fields to match playback problems that viewers see with CloudFront delivery data, which makes troubleshooting faster.

These fields are available in all CloudFront edge locations, and standard logging pricing applies. To learn more, see Standard logging page in the Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide.

According to analysis from Nielsen, streaming represented 49.6 percent of TV viewing in August, with 36.4 percent coming from broadcast and cable. As Netflix seeks to strengthen its lead against rivals like YouTube and Skydance, there’s extra pressure for it to deliver hit indicates and movies.

Sources indicate that I think as Netflix has grown and matured and the business has grown and matured around us, that hit rate really matters. And you’ve got to get ahead of ‘are we on a path to continue [and] maintain that hit rate in the US particularly, but everywhere in the world?’ And I’d say the business is working everywhere in the world, including the US, but we should be doing better in the US than we were. And we’ve got to really focus on our ability to do that.

The CEO said that Netflix is focusing on “the ambition of storytelling” rather than “chasing everything that people just happen to spend five seconds on television on” or relying on AI-generated content.

“I think what’s going to happen is that people will desire more ambitious, more accomplished storytelling in a world that is flooded with slop,” Sarandos said.

Netflix has used generative AI-based workflows for various production tasks, like creating crowds or historical battle scenes, for hundreds of titles. This has helped Netflix save money while it increased the amount it spends on content this year by about 10 percent.

When it comes to streaming consumers struggling to find something to watch, Sarandos acknowledged that Netflix sometimes “make[s] mistakes about how we present latest things” and can “bury things that you might be looking for under new things that you’re not coming for.” He pointed to AI as a tool for content discovery in addition to aiding in the pre-production and post-production of content.

Sources indicate that netflix is also being more open toward theater releases than it has been historically. That change was on the forefront when Netflix was trying to buy Warner Bros. Discovery’s (WBD’s) movie studios business (as well as its streaming business) and convince critics that the acquisition wouldn’t mean fewer theater releases. Although Netflix pulled out of the deal, it’s still eying an increase in theater releases as an opportunity. During the interview, Sarandos noted that the sequel to Netflix’s most popular movie of all time, KPop Demon Hunters (2025), “will be huge in theaters and big on Netflix.” It has also mentioned that it will put movies in theaters for longer and recently extended the scheduled theater release for Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew from two weeks to seven.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Why the best founders are âtime travelersâ who play all three phases simultaneously.

  • In a recent development, in the Prod community, they talk about founders as âtime travelersâ rather than visionaries.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Why the best founders are âtime travelersâ who play all three phases simultaneously.

Why the best founders are âtime travelersâ who play all three phases simultaneously.

In a recent development, in the Prod community, they talk about founders as âtime travelersâ rather than visionaries. Founders donât see the future, they teleport there.

I think this is true in more ways than first meets the eye. To extend the analogy of a chess game (which I recently used in an essay on the AI race and which Will Manidis also articulated beautifully in his essay on âEndgame Playâ), outside observers see startups as temporally sequential, with a beginning (inception/ seed stage), middle (product-market fit/ growth stage), and end (IPO/ scale-up). However, the best founders actually live in all three of these phases simultaneously.

Recent findings suggest that opening: The opening phase of a startup involves the âmagicâ of transforming from a few people with an idea into a âstartup.â Silicon Valley excels at this magic, and Paul Graham is the prophet of the opening. There are many opening strategies, but the lean startup model has proven itself to be the most repeatable one. The ecosystem around company formation is important because foundational decisions made at this stage are difficult to change later, and so wisdom pays dividends.

Recent findings suggest that midgame: The midgame of a startup begins once product-market fit has been reached. Many startups fail before ever reaching this stage. Product-market fit requires deeply understanding a customerâs need, and building a solution. Once product-market fit has been reached, you need to build a tech giant â figure out how to hire people, manage people, and improve the product. You need to achieve some type of takeoff, forward momentum that will allow the business to grow from something tiny and irrelevant into something meaningful and important. Board members exist to transmit inter-generational knowledge on midgame play. Since the nature of the midgame is always evolving, founders need to filter this through their own prism to arrive at truth.

Recent findings suggest that endgame: The endgame of a startup is the infinite future â itâs never really reached. The endgame is important, because without a vision of the future, the present has very little value â see the recent SaaSpocalypse. Elon Musk is the prophet of the endgame, he has always focused on the hardest problems, knowing that ambitious problems attract excellent people and unleash them to do their best work.

Recent findings suggest that some startups seem uniquely engineered for the opening, some for the midgame, and some for the endgame. A hot AI tech giant from Stanford students is engineered for the opening game â they will easily be able to recruit friends and a bike ride to Sand Hill road easily yields capital. A vertical SaaS company is engineered for the midgame â getting off the ground is hard and recruiting the early team is challenging, but once you unlock PMF, thereâs a clear path for how to scale it up. And a deep tech company is engineered for the endgame, itâs always clear from the moment of inception why that company should pass the âwho cares?â test.

Every startup has a different set of challenges depending on what parts of the game are structurally easier and harder. For example, a startup with a weak endgame story will struggle to raise funding without immense traction. A startup with a strong opening story is at risk of hubris, employees thinking the manufacturer has reached the promised land, when nothing substantial has been achieved. And the âvalley of deathâ is famous in deep tech, precisely because a strong endgame story is always preceded by a long, fatigued midgame. The #1 piece of advice I give friends who are starting companies is to be aware of these biases, and explicitly combat them.

According to recent reports, what is so incredible about the best companies, and the best founders, is that they appear to be playing the opening, midgame and endgame simultaneously. In the best companies, it is always early days and there is a significant dream ahead (the opening vibe), even many years in. This is how Clay feels, even though the tech giant is almost ten years old. Similarly, the best startups often have midgame characteristics at the opening â within a few months, they can show traction and improvement, creating a sense of forward momentum. For example, RunwayMLâs incredible open-source growth, years before Stable Diffusion. And finally, the best companies create a feeling of inevitability early, such that employees genuinely feel like they are moving the world forward. For example, Anduril pioneering modern defense tech.

One phrase Iâve often used to describe the best founders is, âNo matter what happens, they are going to win.â Alex Wangâs incredible journey at Scale from strength to strength was an early and illustrative example of this concept for me. The journey of Crusoe from crypto miner to AI factory builder is another great story of grit and judgement. What has crystalized for me now is seeing a superstructure that makes this possible â these founders are constantly holding the opening, midgame and endgame in their minds at the same time, and hence they are able to create a flexible, nimble culture that is always reinventing itself, and they are much quicker in adjusting their business strategy when the times are changing.

My advice to founders is therefore this: No matter where you are in your journey, donât think about your business sequentially. Force yourself to play all three games at once â when planning product decisions, when making hires, when pitching investors. If you are in the midgame, you still need to care about opening style hires that could change the business. If you are in the opening, you need to think about the endgame, because thatâs what will inspire others to join you and help turn your vision into reality. And if you are in the endgame, you should still care about midgame momentum and opening creativity â thatâs how you will become absolutely massive. As you build your organization, each of these narratives should be getting stronger â you canât just focus on the one that seems immediately in front of you.
